author: fester
body: The mutation corpus subject. Deliberately exercises exactly the forms the rechecker examines: a sum with two constructors of different payload types, a match that takes both apart, bounded-integer signatures, a linear parameter, and an effectful function reached from the entry point.

author: fester
body: Payload types differ between the two constructors on purpose. A subject whose constructors both carried Integer could not distinguish a sub-pattern bound at the wrong field type from one bound correctly, which is the property those mutations are aimed at.

author: fester
body: A second sum exists so the corpus can plant a constructor that resolves as a name but does not belong to the sum its reference is typed to build. With one sum type that mutation is indistinguishable from an unbound name, and it was: the arm meant to catch it never ran.

author: fester
body: touch performs port-out-byte, a [Device.Port] intrinsic, while its own signature is pure. That is legal ONLY because this chapter grounds Device.Port, so the mutation that deletes the grounds entry from the wire must come back DISAGREE. Without a grounded def here, the check that consults the table could be deleted outright and the corpus would not notice.

author: fester
body: Everything must be reachable from the entry point or the IR prunes it, so the effectful arm is called rather than merely defined.
